brief.t: Started in 2001 by Chandra Shekhar Ghosh as a microfinance organisation for poor women in rural Bengal; became a universal bank on 23 August 2015.
Founder Ghosh stepped down as MD & CEO in July 2024; ex-SBI and ex-IOB banker Partha Pratim Sengupta has led the bank since 1 November 2024.
Stress in its microfinance (EEB) loans cut profit: FY 2025-26 profit fell to ₹1,224 crore from ₹2,745 crore a year earlier.
Recovery under way: Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit was ₹622 crore, about 5.5 times a year ago, and Gross NPA fell to 3.1% from 5.0%.
Former IRDAI Chairman Debasish Panda is the new Part-time Chairman (RBI approval, April 2026), and the bank launched its first credit cards in Sep 2026.

timeline.t: Bandhan started as a not-for-profit microfinance organisation in Bengal.
Began operations as a universal bank, the first microfinance lender in India to do so.
HDFC-promoted Gruh Finance merged into the bank, adding home loans.
Founder Chandra Shekhar Ghosh stepped down as MD & CEO.
Partha Pratim Sengupta took charge as MD & CEO.
Launched its first credit cards (four variants, on Mastercard).

model.how: Bandhan earns mainly from the interest gap between its loans and deposits. It began with small loans to women in villages (microfinance, now called EEB) and is now growing secured loans such as home loans, vehicle and business loans to reduce risk.
flow: Bank lends: microfinance, home, vehicle, business and retail loans
Earns a wide interest gap + fees

points: Microfinance loans are unsecured and can turn bad quickly when borrowers take too many loans; this hit Bandhan in 2025.
RBI must approve a private bank's MD & CEO and Chairman; both changed at Bandhan in 2024–26.
Big theme for interviews: how a microfinance-born bank diversifies into secured lending.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Microfinance: Small loans, often to women's groups in villages, without collateral. Bandhan calls this business EEB (Emerging Entrepreneurs Business).
glossary.Secured loan: A loan backed by an asset, such as a house or vehicle, that the bank can recover if the borrower does not pay.
glossary.Universal bank: A full-service bank that can offer all banking products to all customers.

Finance.q: Why did Bandhan's FY26 profit fall so much?
Finance.a: Stress in its microfinance (EEB) book raised bad loans and provisions, especially early in the year; profit fell to ₹1,224 cr from ₹2,745 cr.

Finance.q: Why is Bandhan moving towards secured loans?
Finance.a: Unsecured microfinance loans are risky in downturns; home, vehicle and business loans backed by assets make earnings steadier.

Finance.q: Q2 FY27 profit rose 456%. How do you read that?
Finance.a: The year-ago quarter was very weak; lower provisions and 14% NII growth drove the jump. Asset quality must keep improving.

Marketing.q: How would you sell Bandhan's new credit cards?
Marketing.a: Target its existing salaried and small-business customers first, with simple rewards messaging and regional-language campaigns.

Marketing.q: How can Bandhan raise its CASA ratio?
Marketing.a: Salary-account tie-ups, current accounts for small traders, a strong app and cross-selling to loan customers.

HR.q: How would you keep 75,000 employees aligned during leadership changes?
HR.a: Clear communication from the new CEO and Chairman, stable goals, recognition and training on new products.

Sales.q: Sell a Bandhan home loan to a small-town shop owner.
Sales.a: Understand income and documents, explain EMI simply, highlight local branch support and quick processing, then close with a next step.

Operations.q: How would you improve collections in a microfinance branch?
Operations.a: Track early overdue accounts daily, visit borrowers early, use digital payment options and avoid over-lending.

Other.q: What do you know about Bandhan Bank?
Other.a: A Kolkata-based private bank born from microfinance in 2001, a bank since 2015, led by MD & CEO Partha Pratim Sengupta, now recovering with ₹622 cr profit in Q2 FY27.

interview.why_us: Bandhan Bank grew from a small microfinance effort for village women into a bank serving over 3.2 crore customers. After a tough 2025, it is recovering under a new CEO and Chairman, launching credit cards and growing secured loans. Joining during this change means learning fast and seeing real impact. I want to contribute to [your role] as the bank grows stronger.
ask: How is the bank balancing microfinance with secured lending in the next two years?
What has changed in risk and collections since 2025?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.t: Is microfinance good for the poor?
gd.for: It gives small loans to women without collateral and builds livelihoods.
gd.against: Easy credit can lead to over-borrowing and stress, as seen in 2025.

gd.t: Should a founder step back once a company grows big?
gd.for: Fresh leadership can bring new skills; Bandhan now has an ex-SBI banker as CEO.
gd.against: Founders understand the mission and customers best.

avoid: Don't name Chandra Shekhar Ghosh as current CEO; he stepped down in July 2024. Partha Pratim Sengupta leads now.
Don't call Bandhan a microfinance company or NBFC; it has been a universal bank since 2015.
Don't quote the 456% growth without context: the year-ago quarter was very weak.
